transcript.text: We replaced our old condenser dryer with a heat pump one about a month ago and honestly it's driving me mad, a normal load of towels takes nearly 3 and a half hours, the old one did it in about 90 minutes. It also feels barely warm for the first half hour when I open the door to check. Surely that's not right? Is it faulty?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. Probably not. Heat-pump dryers run at a lower temperature and take much longer than condenser dryers, so a long cycle that starts barely warm is typical. This sounds like normal behaviour rather than a fault: Heat-pump dryers dry at a lower temperature and take noticeably longer than vented or condenser dryers; clothes come out warm rather than hot. It would be worth a closer look if clothes are still wet at the end of a full cycle with clean filters and an emptied water tank. Is it genuinely cold and never drying, or does it dry but just feels cooler / slower than your old dryer?
It does dry them in the end, clothes come out fully dry. It's just the time it takes, and it only feels lukewarm to start with. So is 3 and a half hours really normal for a load of towels?

Yes, for a heat pump dryer that's normal: they dry at a much lower temperature than your old condenser dryer, so they feel only lukewarm, especially at the start, and a full load of towels can easily take around 3 to 3. 5 hours. Then no repair is needed. If it ever does it in a way that does not fit that, get back in touch and we will look further.
